title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused ROPE ops + scheduling/KV-cache tuning
author: Wei Zhang
description:
Motivation: replace legacy attention kernels with FlashAttentionV2 and add a fused ROPE/rotary update to reduce memory traffic and improve throughput for long-context workloads. This PR also adds a small kernel-selection shim and scheduler hints so the serving runtime can pick the best kernel variant at runtime (v2, v2+fused-rope, or fallback) and adjusts KV-cache layout to avoid an extra copy for fused variants.

What changed (high level):
- Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels (CUDA) with a new ABI shim that supports optional fused ROPE preprocessing.
- Implement fused ROPE/rotary application inside the attention kernels to avoid separate elementwise ops and reduce global memory reads.
- Add runtime kernel selector heuristics: selects fused variant for QKV shapes and GPU SMs where it shows win; otherwise picks FlashAttentionV2 or fallback. Selector factors: sm_arch, head_dim, batch*seq, available shared memory.
- Adjust KV cache layout (rope-aware kv layout) to enable direct indexing into the fused kernel without intermediate transpose/copy.
- Update continuous-batching scheduler to attach kernel hints to batches and avoid mixing incompatible variants in the same microbatch.
- Add unit and integration tests for numerical parity (float32/float16) and a perf benchmark harness used in CI perf-suite.

Benchmarks:
- Internal perf runs on A10G: ~1.25x throughput improvement on 8k context, 1.4x on 16k when fused-rope applies, latency P95 reduced by ~12% for common request sizes.
- Memory: peak GPU memory decreased by ~8% for fused path due to fewer temporaries.

Backwards compatibility & rollout:
- Default behavior is to enable fused kernels on supported GPUs only; feature gate and environment variable REDWOOD_ENABLE_FUSED_ROPE allow disabling for canary.
- Adds safe fallback path to prior FlashAttention implementation (v1 emulation) when build-time or runtime capability checks fail.

Testing & CI:
- Added new CI job perf-suite/gpu that runs microbenchmarks on internal GPU runners; CPU unit tests run on every push.
- Numerical tolerance checks included; added a repro test that runs the transformer block forward/backward for short/long sequences.

Migration notes:
- Operators exposing kernel selection are behind a feature flag; Dedicated customers can opt-in. Private installer automatically enables for clusters with supported CUDA drivers.

Related: ENG-1574 (serving perf initiative), ENG-1622 (continuous-batcher improvements).
